newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia appoints new board of ailing Rijeka port.
newsitem.headline: Croatia appoints new board of ailing Rijeka port.

text.p: The Croatian government on Monday appointed a new board to take charge of the ailing Rijeka port company with Ante Dropulic as acting director, the state news agency Hina reported.
It quoted Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavec as saying at a news conference that the reshuffle was needed to rehabilitate the company after the previous management failed to prevent deep losses.
Dropulic has spent 20 years working for Rijeka port, including 11 years as its financial director.
The company's debt is estimated at 160 million kuna ($24.4 million) and new management faces tough negotiations with debtors before it is ready for privatisation, Luzavec said.
Handling of cargo fell to 2.3 million tonnes last year from 3.7 million in 1995. It shrank to a mere 110,000 tonnes by June this year.
Luzavec singled out poor traffic links between Rijeka and the interior, inadequate storage space and restructuring as the most burning problems.
But a motorway to Budapest via the capital Zagreb, due to be finished by 1999, is expected to improve its prospects.

Several foreign investors, including Korea's Samsung Corp. have expressed readiness to participate in upgrading the port capacities. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.558 Croatian Kuna)
